bull_bear.body: Focus on debottlenecking and specialty capacity utilization; No dividend/buyback commentary in transcript; Working capital management critical due to elevated raw material prices.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Prolonged West Asia conflict affecting Strait of Hormuz (Sulfur/Ethylene Oxide supply); Demand destruction from inflationary consumer spending; Currency volatility in AMET (Egypt/Turkey); Grammage reduction by customers as alternative to price hikes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously Optimistic; Emphasizes agility in supply chain management; Transparent about Q4 logistics headwinds; Confident in Q1 recovery trajectory based on order backlog and India resilience.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: AMET volume decline (-15%) was almost entirely supply-constrained (March shutdown) rather than demand-led; Excluding March, AMET growth would have been +2-3%; Panic buying denied by management, inventory builds were for security of supply amid price hikes.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Breadth of portfolio and customer reach — over 215 products supplied to more than 1,500 customers across 95+ countries
- Diversified, strategically located manufacturing footprint across India, Egypt and the United States supporting a resilient supply chain
- Four decades of operating history and trust/credibility built with customers and partners since 1980
- Deep formulation and application expertise enabling next-generation platforms such as GALSORB® SunBliss and Galsoft® Lumithic
- Dedicated D2C vertical offering concept-to-prototype development, customised formulation, technical guidance, regulatory awareness and commercialisation support to emerging brands
- Diversified geographic mix — stable ROW performance and Tier-2/Tier-3 growth in India offset the AMET decline in FY26
- Digital and process discipline — global HRMS rollout and over 50 standardised workflows with automated reporting frameworks
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global geopolitical conflict and trade/tariff disruption — Escalation of conflicts in the Middle East and Red Sea can disrupt global supply chains and trade routes, while the trade tariff war between major economies such as the US and China creates uncertainty and could lead to increased costs and supply chain disruptions.
- Feedstock and critical raw-material availability — Unavailability or constrained availability of key feedstocks/critical raw materials, or slower-than-expected demand recovery, may bear on volumes and adversely impact FY2027 performance.
- Raw-material price volatility in fatty alcohol and petrochemical inputs — Fatty Alcohol and Fatty Acids account for the majority of raw material purchases and are sourced from South East Asia; these markets stayed structurally tight and elevated on feedstock constraints, capacity dynamics and geopolitical disruption, while petrochemical feedstocks saw sharp cost pressure late in the year on elevated crude prices.
- Gestation risk on new launches and premium specialty restocking — Although the destocking cycle has ended, delay in new launches or a slower-than-expected restocking/recovery cycle in Premium specialties will adversely impact profitability going ahead.
- Logistics — container availability, freight cost and lead times — Container unavailability, a sudden increase in freight costs, or increased lead times from sudden route changes as seen during the Red Sea crisis pose risk to volumes and overall profitability.
- Climate risk and monsoon dependence of Indian demand — Delayed or below-average monsoons in India may halt growth momentum since rural recovery is a critical requisite for Indian demand; climatic catastrophes pose an unquantifiable risk to global supply chains and adversely impact consumption.
- Employee safety, health and process-safety incidents — A BRSR-identified material issue: risk of process safety incidents and occupational health hazards, mitigated through ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 implementation, Process Safety Management, Behaviour-Based Safety programmes, regular audits, training and Board oversight.
- Water scarcity and water stewardship — A BRSR-identified material issue: risk from water scarcity and climate variability, mitigated through Zero Liquid Discharge facilities, rainwater harvesting, recycling, water-usage monitoring, ISO 46001:2019 implementation and community water projects.
- Cyber threats arising from digitalisation — A BRSR-identified material issue: risk of cyber threats alongside the opportunity to enhance efficiency and decision-making, addressed through investments in IT infrastructure, cybersecurity controls and digital tools.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Vision 2030: to delight customers, be a partner of choice and a global leader of surfactants and specialty chemicals to the Home, Beauty Care, Wellness and Personal Care industries, with a commitment to a cleaner and safer environment.
- Bolster existing capacities operationally while selectively expanding geographic reach and deepening presence in priority markets, building on established strength in India and other international markets.
- Drive specialty growth and premiumisation, supported by agile customer engagement and proactive management of supply-chain and cost dynamics.
- Broaden the customer base beyond Tier-1 accounts to Tier-2/Tier-3, emerging brands and direct-to-consumer players, including a dedicated D2C vertical acting as co-creator from concept to shelf.
- Rebranding to 'Chemistry Creates Care' as a strategic investment within the Vision 2030 journey — to strengthen customer relationships, attract future-ready talent and accelerate sustainable growth.
- GIFT (Galaxy Industry 4.0 Transformation): integrate Operational Technology and Information Technology for autonomous, connected, data-driven manufacturing, with a vision to digitise all factories by 2030 (eLogbooks, Electronic Batch Manufacturing Records, IoT-enabled real-time equipment monitoring).
- Mission Shunya — flagship safety initiative aimed at achieving zero harm to people, assets and the environment, with continued strengthening of process safety capabilities.
- Embed sustainability in strategy and operations — solar/renewable electricity, water recycling and rainwater harvesting, RSPO Mass Balance certified sourcing and waste circularity.
- CSR platforms as durable community programmes: Gyan Sanjeevani (education), Aarogya Vardheeni (health), Samajeek Utthaan (rural development), Paryavaran Suraksha (environment) and Stree Unnati (women empowerment).
- Certified under ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 50001, ISO 46001 (GSL Taloja), ISO 10002, ISO 27001 and ISO 14064, along with RSPO, ISCC Plus and VDF.
- Member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) and follows ISCC Plus and VDF standards to promote sustainable sourcing; supplies RSPO Mass Balance certified products and engages customers on sustainable sourcing.
- Signatory to the Responsible Care Global Charter (RCGC), covering health, safety, environmental protection and ethical conduct.
- Sustainability disclosures prepared in accordance with GRI Standards, with assurance based on the AA1000 framework; Bureau Veritas (India) Private Limited provides Reasonable Assurance on the BRSR.
- Participates in EcoVadis (Environment, Labour & Human Rights, Ethics, Sustainable Procurement) and the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP), reporting on climate change, water security, biodiversity, plastics and forests.
- All manufacturing sites are audited under SEDEX SMETA 4-pillar (Labour Standards, Health & Safety, Environment, Business Ethics).
- Water stewardship through Zero Liquid Discharge facilities, rainwater harvesting, recycling, water-usage monitoring, ISO 46001:2019 implementation and community water projects.
- Waste management via TPM, WESAP, CEP, waste segregation, recycling initiatives, disposal through authorised agencies and employee engagement programmes.
- Increased renewable energy usage, energy efficiency projects and performance monitoring to reduce emissions and energy costs.
- Board-level Risk Management Committee with an enterprise risk framework and ethics mechanisms.
- Structured customer complaint management using 8D methodology with continuous improvement actions.
- Great Place to Work Certification for people practices, and listed on The Valuable 500 platform with a CEO-level commitment to disability inclusion.
- Board-approved policies covering all nine NGRBC principles, translated into procedures and extended to value chain partners.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report does not name any individual plant, line or capacity project with a commissioning date. Expansion is framed through Vision 2030, articulated at the Company's Capital Market Day, which builds on the philosophy of investing ahead of the curve in products, people and infrastructure followed by phases of superior performance. The Vision has been expanded to explicitly include Beauty & Wellness alongside the core Home and Personal Care focus — an expansion within the core rather than a diversification away from it — enabling entry into faster-growing, premium and innovation-led segments such as skincare, sun care and derma-based actives. Five strategic levers underpin growth: premiumisation and penetration, expansion into new categories and applications, deeper engagement with D2C brands and private labels, strengthening sustainability and clean beauty capabilities, and leveraging partnerships and inorganic opportunities. The portfolio shift runs from traditional rinse-off strengths (hair care, bath and shower, oral care) toward leave-on segments (skincare, sun care, cosmetics, derma), which carry higher innovation intensity, greater technical complexity and superior margin profiles. Regionally the Company runs a Defend & Grow strategy in India and AMET, and a Challenge & Penetrate / 'winning' strategy in the Americas (leveraging the TRI-K platform) and Europe (specialty-led growth supported by localisation and increased on-ground presence). Capital allocation is disciplined and balanced: a significant portion of operating cash flows is directed to organic growth including capacity expansion, innovation and capability building, while maintaining adequate headroom for inorganic initiatives such as acquisitions and strategic partnerships, alongside continued shareholder returns through dividends and a strong, resilient balance sheet. The stated Vision 2030 financial aspirations are a doubling of volumes, 2.5 times growth in EBITDA, and sustained return on capital employed of over 22 percent.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Medium-term fundamentals for the personal and home care industry remain robust, particularly in emerging markets such as India, even as the near-term environment stays shaped by geopolitical uncertainty, inflationary pressures and financial market volatility.
- India growth was led by strong momentum in the masstige specialty ingredients portfolio; performance surfactants saw softer demand from a large customer due to reformulation initiatives linked to elevated input costs, partly offset by emerging brands and D2C players.
- AMET remained challenging — Middle East geopolitical disruption in March affected logistics and inventory cycles, and lower offtake from certain key customers amid intensifying local competition.
- Rest of the World was steady, with continued strength in specialty ingredients across APAC and Latin America; Europe subdued; North America pressured mid-year by tariff dynamics before recovering on improved customer engagement and premium specialty momentum at TRI-K, USA.
- Fatty Alcohol and Fatty Acids account for the majority of raw material purchases, with fatty alcohol sourced from South East Asia (Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand); these markets stayed structurally tight and elevated through the year on feedstock constraints, capacity dynamics and geopolitical disruption.
- Petrochemical feedstocks were relatively stable for most of the year but saw sharp cost pressure towards the end on supply disruptions and elevated crude prices.
- Crude oil is expected to stay elevated and volatile in 2026 (IMF base case around $82/bbl, World Bank about $86/bbl, with upside to $100–125 in disruption scenarios) before moderating to around $70 by 2027 as supply normalises.
- FY27 outlook: cautiously optimistic, with early indicators pointing to recovery in India underpinned by resilient consumption and increasing momentum in specialty and premium segments; LATAM and APAC showing signs of improvement.
- In the United States, the reversal of earlier tariff measures is expected to open incremental opportunities in specialty care ingredients, supporting traction in higher-value offerings.
- For AMET, the evolving geopolitical situation in West Asia remains a key area of focus for regional demand, feedstock availability, logistics networks and broader supply chains.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Q4FY26 EBITDA declined 9.6% YoY to INR 122 Cr due to West Asia war-induced logistics bottlenecks and feedstock inflation, though India resilience (8% vol growth) and US tariff reversals provide a clear Q1FY27 recovery path. Management guides Q1 volume growth to 6-8% (higher end) and EBITDA/ton to INR 19k-21k (higher end), signaling a sequential inflection as Egypt operations normalize and specialty pipelines re-accelerate.

open.item: The Board has recommended a final dividend of ₹ 22 per equity share for FY26, to be approved at the Fortieth Annual General Meeting on August 12, 2026.
Management flags that unavailability or constrained availability of key feedstocks/critical raw materials, or slower-than-expected demand recovery, may adversely impact FY2027 performance.

For FY27 the Company is cautiously optimistic on a recovery in India led by resilient consumption and specialty/premium momentum, with LATAM and APAC improving and US tariff reversal expected to open incremental opportunities in specialty care ingredients.
Under the GIFT (Galaxy Industry 4.0 Transformation) initiative, the Company is guided by a clear vision to digitise all factories by 2030.
Vision 2030 financial aspiration of doubling volumes.
Vision 2030 financial aspiration of 2.5 times growth in EBITDA.
Vision 2030 aspiration of sustained return on capital employed of over 22 percent.

Expand the Vision to include Beauty & Wellness alongside Home and Personal Care, enabling entry into skincare, sun care and derma-based actives — an expansion within the core value chain rather than a diversification away from it.
The Company will continue to invest in scalable platforms, future-focused capability building and leadership development to strengthen organisational resilience.
The Company remains committed to Mission Shunya — achieving zero harm to people, assets and the environment — and to strengthening its process safety capabilities.

Management flags that while the destocking cycle has ended, delay in new launches or a slower-than-expected restocking/recovery cycle in Premium specialties will adversely impact profitability going ahead.
The Company intends to actively pursue partnerships, alliances and targeted acquisitions to accelerate entry into new technologies, markets and segments, particularly within Beauty & Wellness.

A significant portion of operating cash flows will be allocated to organic growth including capacity expansion, innovation and capability building, while maintaining adequate headroom for inorganic initiatives and continuing shareholder returns through dividends with a strong balance sheet.
